subject: Copying Scale from one plot to another

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Copying Scale from one plot to another
parts:
Dears, 

Trying to finalize a plot that I'm making. Essentially, I loop through columns of data and plot a histogram of the entire dataset and then inset a pair of plots which are a subset of the original set (essentially controls). 

The trouble is that when I subset the data and plot, I get a different scale from the main image. Here is a simple (mostly) example:

set.seed(1)
grp1<-data.frame(variable= "grp1", value=rnorm(120, 100, 25))
grp2<-data.frame(variable= "grp2", value=rnorm(120, 200, 35))
others<-data.frame(variable= "others", value=rnorm(660, 150, 100))
raw.data<-rbind(grp1, grp2, others)

standard.names<-c("grp1", "grp2")

raw.data.standard<-raw.data[raw.data[["variable"]] %in% standard.names,]

main_plot<-
ggplot()+
geom_histogram(data=raw.data, aes(x=value))+
theme_bw()

inset_plot<-
ggplot()+
geom_histogram(data=raw.data.standard, aes(x = value))+
facet_wrap(~ variable,  nrow=1)

#save plots
png(filename = "junk.png", width = 6, height = 6, units = "in", res=400)
grid.newpage()
vp_main<-viewport(width = 1, height = 1, x = 0.5, y = 0.5)
vp_inset<-viewport(width = 0.4, height = 0.2, x = 0.3, y = 0.87)
print(main_plot, vp = vp_main)
print(inset_plot, vp = vp_inset)
dev.off()

Is there a way to ensure that the x-axis scale/ticks of the insets match the x-axis of the main histogram? 

Thanks, 

Brandon

parts:
How about this ? A bit dirty though!! 

 
<..code blocks>
raw.data.standard<-raw.data[raw.data[["variable"]] %in% standard.names,]

## get the default number of breaks from the graphics `hist` function. 
breaks_of_histogram = hist(raw.data$value, plot = FALSE)$breaks

## get the range of the breaks_of_histogram 
range_of_breaks = range(breaks_of_histogram)

## set the limits. 
xlimits = xlim(range_of_breaks[1], range_of_breaks[2])

main_plot<-
ggplot()+
geom_histogram(data=raw.data, aes(x=value))+
theme_bw() + xlimits

inset_plot<-
ggplot()+
geom_histogram(data=raw.data.standard, aes(x = value))+

facet_wrap(~ variable,  nrow=1) + xlimits

<.. code blocks.. >

messages.subject: Re: Copying Scale from one plot to another
parts:
Hi Brandon,

You can extract the information from the main plot, like this:

x.range <- ggplot_build(main_plot)$panel$ranges[[1]]$x.range

Then

grid.newpage()
vp_main<-viewport(width = 1, height = 1, x = 0.5, y = 0.5)
vp_inset<-viewport(width = 0.4, height = 0.2, x = 0.3, y = 0.87)
print(main_plot, vp = vp_main)

print(inset_plot + xlim(x.range), vp = vp_inset)

should give you the same x-axis on the main and sub plots.

Best,
Ista

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Copying Scale from one plot to another
parts:
Dears, 

Dennis gave me some help offlist too. The final solution was to do what Abhishek suggested, but using a function the scales package called pretty_breaks(). Once fixed to the range of the entire dataset it wasn't complicated. ggplot_build() would have worked, but I worry about using it because it could change at any time. 

Thanks to all for your responses!

Final code for plot below:
require(plyr)
require(agricolae)
require(gridExtra)
require(grid)
require(ggplot2)
require(scales)

#### Theme for inset plot, reduces all unnecessary space and just prints the plot
theme_inset <- function (base_size = 12, base_family = ""){
  theme_bw (base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family) %+replace% 
     theme(
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(0.3)),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(0.5)),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(), 
    axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
    axis.title.y = element_blank(), 
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0, "lines"), 
    axis.ticks.margin = unit(0, "lines"), 
    legend.position = "none", 
    #panel.background = element_blank(), 
    panel.border = element_blank(), 
    #panel.grid.major = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
    panel.margin = unit(0, "lines"), 
    plot.background = element_blank(), 
    plot.margin = unit(c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), "lines"),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_blank()
    )

}



set.seed(1)
grp1<-data.frame(variable= "grp1", value=rnorm(120, 100, 25))
grp2<-data.frame(variable= "grp2", value=rnorm(120, 200, 35))
others<-data.frame(variable= "others", value=rnorm(660, 150, 100))
raw.data<-rbind(grp1, grp2, others)

standard.names<-c("grp1", "grp2")
raw.data.standard<-raw.data[raw.data[["variable"]] %in% standard.names,]

raw.data.standard.avg<- ddply(raw.data.standard, "variable", colwise(mean, na.rm=T))

capture.output(aov.test<-aov(value ~ variable, data=raw.data.standard))
capture.output(anova.pval<-summary(aov.test)[[1]]$'Pr(>F)'[1])
capture.output(Ptable<-LSD.test(aov.test, trt="variable")$means)
Ptable<-data.frame(trt=substr(row.names(Ptable), 1,6), Ptable)

capture.output(Gtable<-LSD.test(aov.test, trt="variable")$groups)
Gtable$trt<-substr(Gtable$trt, 1,6)

alltable<-merge(Ptable, Gtable, all=T)
finaltable<-data.frame(Name= alltable[["trt"]], n=alltable[["r"]], mean = round(alltable[[2]], 2), SEM=round(alltable[[3]], 2), LSDGroup = alltable[[10]])

#compute range and breaks to fix things between main and inset plots
plot.breaks<-pretty_breaks(n=5)(raw.data[["value"]])
plot.range<-range(plot.breaks)

main_plot<-
ggplot()+
geom_histogram(data=raw.data, aes(x=value))+

geom_blank(data=raw.data, aes(x=value, y=1.2*..count..), stat="bin")+ # creates a 20% buffer at the top of the plot for adding the controls
geom_vline(data=raw.data.standard.avg, aes(xintercept = value, color= variable))+
geom_text(data=raw.data.standard.avg, aes(x= value, y= 0, label= variable), angle=90, colour="grey48", hjust=0, vjust=0, size=2)+
annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, label = paste("ANOVA of Standards p ≤ ", round(anova.pval, 2), sep = ""), size=2.5, hjust=1, vjust=1)+
scale_x_continuous(limits= plot.range, breaks=plot.breaks)+

theme_bw()

inset_plot<-
ggplot()+
geom_histogram(data=raw.data.standard, aes(x= value))+

geom_vline(data=raw.data.standard.avg, aes(xintercept = value, color= variable), size=0.25)+
facet_wrap(~variable,  nrow=1)+
geom_text(data = raw.data.standard, aes(x= -Inf, y=Inf, label = substr(variable, 1, 6)), size = 3, hjust=0, vjust=1)+
scale_x_continuous(limits= plot.range, breaks=plot.breaks)+
theme_inset()

#save plots
png(filename = "junk.png", width = 6, height = 6, units = "in", res=400)
grid.newpage()
vp_main<-viewport(width = 1, height = 1, x = 0.5, y = 0.5)
vp_inset<-viewport(width = 0.4, height = 0.2, x = 0.3, y = 0.87)
print(main_plot, vp = vp_main)
print(inset_plot, vp = vp_inset)
dev.off()
